text:
**Chosen Method:** FDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]
**Justification:** FDISCO is selected because it is specifically optimized to preserve endogenous fluorescence (like tdTomato) in solvent-based clearing by using pH-adjusted reagents, which prevents the quenching typically seen in iDISCO. It is significantly faster than aqueous methods (like CUBIC) and induces tissue shrinkage, which is advantageous for rapid whole-brain imaging of long-range projections using light-sheet microscopy. β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) is a robust marker for the axonal cytoskeleton.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Dehydration
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) THF (diluted in distilled water, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF (diluted in distilled water, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF (diluted in distilled water, pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (pH adjusted to 9.0 with triethylamine). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)
2 RI Matching and Clearing
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Dibenzyl ether) until the tissue becomes transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)
3 Preservation and Pre-imaging
3.1 Storage in fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a dark, airtight glass vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)
3.2 Mounting in a light-sheet microscope imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: 0.5 hours)
